fn solve(n: Int, m: Int, tasks: List[Int]) -> Int
  requires (n >= 2)
  requires (m >= 1)
  requires (len(tasks) == m)
  requires forall i in 0..len(tasks): ((1 <= tasks[i]) and (tasks[i] <= n))
  ensures (result >= 0)
  ensures ((not (m > 0)) or (result >= (tasks[(m - 1)] - 1)))
  ensures (result <= ((((m - 1) * n) + tasks[(m - 1)]) - 1))
  effects pure
  example (solve(0, 0, []) == 0)
